newsitem.title: FRANCE: Thomson sale terms to be set by end of week.
newsitem.headline: Thomson sale terms to be set by end of week.

text.p: New terms for the privatisation sales of French electronics group Thomson SA will be announced by the end of the week, official sources said on Tuesday.
The French government last Wednesday suspended a planned sale of the company to Groupe and Daewoo Electronics of South Korea.
"The aim of the government is to announce new terms between now and the end of the week," an official source said.
Sources close to the matter said that a statement could even be made as soon as Wednesday or Thursday before President Jacques Chirac's televised interview in the evening.

Prime Minister Alain Juppe said on Monday that it was a possibility the group's 58-percent stake in defence electronics group Thomson-CSF and the fully-owned consumer electronics unit Thomson Multimedia would be sold seperately.
In February, announcing the original sale plans, Chirac said the Thomson group needed to be sold as one entity.
The government announced on October 16 it had preferred an offer by Lagardere over one by Alcatel-Alsthom.
France would have sold indebted Thomson SA for one franc to Lagardere after an 10.8 billion franc capital increase.
Lagardere would then have sold Thomson Multimedia, also for one franc, to Daewoo.
But the independent seven-member Privatisation Commission said it had objections to terms of the sale to Daewoo, effectively blocking the privatisation plans.
